status: version 2: stage S0 as in version 1 (run and passed), and the main study on the capture fixed here before any read of the capture
question: does a small MDQR (a queue-reactive book whose intensities come from a neural network of the state, after Bodor and Carlier, arXiv 2501.08822v1) fix what #286 found for the fitted QR model (transient, queues climbing to the cap, worse than its constant baseline on queue TV) without artefacts, and do #102's policies transfer to it
approval: design note v0 (bus 61956), approved with changes (bus 61960): the Hyperliquid capture is the main data, synthetic QR days only as stage S0; K = 3 with the gap from the paper's 5 stated; current QR and its constant baseline are the controls, without waiting for #290; #102's policies transfer at their own execution
paper_gap: the paper models 5 limits a side on FGBL futures, MLP 256-64 tanh, sizes 1 to 200; here K = 3 (the replay's declared depth, #263), MLP 128-64 tanh, sizes 1 to 64 in event-size units, and in S0 the truth's own 2 limits; no code was released with the paper, so this is a reimplementation from its text

s0.purpose: a control on synthetic data where QR is the truth: MDQR fitted on the truth's events must recover it, before any fit on the capture
s0.data: SYNTHETIC: the queue-reactive simulator at #102's calm parameters (experiments/m4_06/design.json, pinned below), not market data

seeds.rule: fixed here before any run; a window is one run of the simulator from a book drawn from the invariant laws

model.mechanics: the queue-reactive book of src/backtest/queue_reactive.rs: an event moves one queue by one event size; a mid move while the opposite first queue is empty moves the reference with probability theta, shifts the queues one limit with the event-size renormalization, and redraws the book from the invariant laws with probability theta_reinit; the same xorshift64* generator, so that with the truth's own intensities the model is the simulator event for event (a test)
model.intensity: an MLP 128-64 tanh of the state to the log intensities of the 3 kinds x 2 sides x 2 limits; an intensity is 0 where the state forbids the event (a cancel or market order on an empty queue, a limit order on a full one)
model.state: log(1 + queue) of each queue (4), the spread in ticks, the kind of the last event at each queue (one-hot, 4 x 4 with none), and the time since the last event at each queue, log(1 + seconds); no hour, since S0's windows have no time of day
model.sizes: every S0 event moves a queue by one event size, so the size head is not used in S0; it is fitted on the capture only
model.clock: continuous: S0's events have distinct times, so the block clock with the end-of-block token, needed for the capture's block-tied times, is not used in S0
model.mechanics_parameters: theta, theta_reinit and the invariant laws estimated from the training windows (the share of eligible moves that moved, of moves that redrew, and the queue sizes at the samples, per limit, sides pooled)
model.fit: maximum likelihood of the marked point process: for each event, log intensity of the event at the state before it, less the total intensity times the time since the previous event; Adam, learning rate 0.001, minibatch 4096, 8 epochs over the training windows' events, float64, torch with 1 thread
model.simulation_seeds: the evaluation windows' seeds, so each model window is drawn as the truth's window of the same index is

s0.comparison: compare_trajectories (src/backtest/queue_reactive.rs) of each model or truth_again window against the evaluation window of the same index, at flow_interval_ms; per window and per training seed
s0.stop_rule: MDQR passes S0 if, for every training seed, its mean over the evaluation windows of the queue size TV at each limit, and of the flow law TV for each kind, is at most the truth's self-discrepancy (truth_again against evaluation, the same mean) plus 0.05; else the study stops and reports that MDQR cannot recover the truth
s0.compute: 0 job slots: CPU torch, 1 thread, in this window's share; an estimate is recorded after a timing pilot of one seed on one window

data.label: REAL DATA: the public Hyperliquid Order Flow Dataset, BTC perpetual, December 2025 (Zenodo 18184441, version 1.0, CC BY 4.0), as recorded on #76; Hyperliquid only, never mixed with another dataset
data.archives: the raw archives at /Users/joaquin/Downloads/hyperliquid_202512, read only: book_diffs_202512.tar (sha256 b95f6166…13e8ec), btc_orders_202512.tar.xz (7bee8701…c9d4), trades_2025_12.tar (f2fbb81f…50cc, checked 2026-11-08)
data.members: every hour of the epoch's replay, 2025-12-21 h15 to 2025-12-30 h18 UTC (220 hours), each as its three files o/<day>/btc_<hh>.data, d/<day>/ex<h> and t/<day>/<h>, gunzipped into /Users/joaquin/tmp/worktrees/market-maker-rs/m5_01_data/; each file's sha256 is checked against #76's per-file manifest (2232 lines, sha256 94752eb07b5a4ad101806654704764489b60e9916e3ff2af234597ba2554a337) before it is read, and the report states that every file matched; the directory is deleted after the holdout
data.replay: src/backtest/hyperliquid.rs as examples/hyperliquid_validation.rs runs it (#263): tick 1, limits K = 3, a reset on a silence over 60 s, a warm-up of 10 minutes, book samples every 1 s; the hours are ingested in order from h15 of 2025-12-21, the file holding the reset at 15:03:26

epoch.why: the longest reset-free stretch of the month, warm after the reset at 15:03:26 and its 10 minute warm-up, as #263 and #290 used (bus 62810)

split.rule: hyperliquid_validation's Protocol: training 600 per mille, validation 200, holdout the rest, by time, each boundary rounded down to a whole second; the first 100 per mille of training, at most 1 h, estimates the event sizes, and the rest is the queue fit's training
split.check: the extractor computes the split with Protocol from the replay's own epoch and refuses to go on if it differs from these boundaries

windows.rule: 2 h windows, fixed here; a window's events and samples come from the continuous replay, so its book carries its history
windows.why: MDQR trains on one 2 h window a training day (the full stretch, about 10 M events a day, is too many for CPU training at this budget); QR, Hawkes and Poisson fit on the whole queue_train as #263 does, so the controls are as strong as they were; the holdout's first window is #263's out-of-sample book window
windows.disclosed: #286 already compared QR and its constant baseline with the data on #263's holdout book window, and #290 read the training part; MDQR's fit and every MDQR figure are new, but the holdout is not unseen for the QR arms

arms.qr: #90's estimate on queue_train, as #263 fits it (ZeroWaitPolicy Drop, the default); #290 found it transient, so S1's cap rule is read for it too and reported
arms.qr_constant: its constant baseline (#286), the only stationary QR model on this window per #290
arms.hawkes: fit_hawkes on queue_train's first-limit segments, the decay chosen on validation from [0.1, 1, 10, 100] as #263 does
arms.mdqr: MDQR-small at K = 3: the QR book's mechanics (theta, theta_reinit and the invariant laws estimated on the mdqr_train windows), an intensity network MLP 128-64 tanh, a size network MLP 128-64 tanh over sizes 1 to 64 event sizes (64 meaning 64 or more), 5 training seeds

clock.blocks: events at one timestamp form a block (80 to 89 % of waits are zero on the capture, #290: 54.9 events a block); the network's total intensity is the block rate, and a block's events are a sequence: after each event the state updates and the network chooses the next event or an end-of-block token, so no event is dropped
clock.likelihood: the block's waiting time under the block rate at the state after the previous block, plus the cross-entropy of each event and of the end token within the block, plus each event's size under the size network
clock.zero_waits: QR is fitted as #90 does (zero waits dropped), the comparison #290 found transient; MDQR's block clock is the stated alternative

main_study.state: log(1 + queue) of the 6 queues in event sizes, the spread in ticks, the signed trade imbalance over the last 20 s, 1 min, 5 min and 15 min, the kind of the last event at each queue, the time since it, and the hour of the day as sine and cosine
main_study.fit: as S0: Adam, learning rate 0.001, minibatch 4096 blocks, 8 epochs, float64, torch with 1 thread, seeds 1 to 5; early stopping on the validation windows' log-likelihood, at most 8 epochs, the epoch kept fixed before any holdout read
main_study.generative_metrics: per holdout window, each arm's simulation from the window's starting book against the data: compare_trajectories (queue size TV per limit, spread TV, waiting KS, flow law TV, coverage), best bid and ask queue correlation, P(kind | queue, limit) TV, next mid move balanced accuracy, gamma shape of queue sizes, share of events at the cap; 2000 block bootstrap replicates over the 3 windows' 10 min blocks, mean block 2, seed 106

transfer.rule: #102's frozen arms (Avellaneda-Stoikov, GLFT, fixed spread, maskable PPO seeds 1 to 5, residual SAC seeds 1 to 5) run on each generator's rows at #102's own execution: 10 s rows, queue_position_rational at 1 lot per 5000 ms, min_queue 0, #102's fee, latency and limits (bus 61960); rows from a generator's sampled book at 10 s, top of book in kernel ticks and lots
transfer.check: before any transfer run, on a validation window's generated rows, a classical arm fills and its net differs from immediate fill
transfer.read: each policy's net per generator, the Kendall tau of the policies' ranking under MDQR against under QR and against the data's own rows, with bootstrap intervals; rows do not react to the policy's orders, as in #102

stop_rules.S1: on validation, MDQR is discarded if it produces a NaN or more than 1 % of its events at the cap in 24 simulated hours; reported with the failure mode
stop_rules.S2: adopted only if on the holdout its queue size TV beats both QR and the constant baseline at every limit with intervals excluding zero, no dependency metric is worse than QR's interval, and the transfer tau against QR is at least 0.6; else discarded with the evidence

main_study.compute: extraction and replay at 0 job slots, one process; MDQR training 5 seeds on 2 slots once granted (bus 62495), announced on the bus; an estimate from a timing pilot of one seed on one training window, recorded in changes before the other fits
